title: Adaptive Cohort Guardrails and Decision Flow for Optimize Eval Quality
creator: Amina Patel
description: This PRD defines an adaptive, hypothesis-driven evaluation contract for Redwood Optimize that: 1) assigns traffic-safe signals to cohorted prompt sets, 2) computes multi-signal regression scores with dynamic thresholds, and 3) maps those signals to automated and manual rollback actions. The goal is to reduce false positives that trigger unnecessary rollbacks while ensuring real regressions are caught quickly and acted on with clear playbooks for engineers and SREs. This work is specifically for the Optimize product: the eval harness and production canaries that gate model/quantization rollouts.
background: Customers using Optimize rely on automated recommendations (quantization, batching, model variants). We currently lack a unified eval contract that ties prompt cohorts, statistical tests, and actionability rules to a deterministic rollback flow. Recent outages (INC-2026-09) highlighted oscillations from over-sensitive single-signal thresholds which rolled back benign changes. This PRD aims to codify a stable multi-signal approach and explicit decision flow to avoid both missed regressions and noisy rollbacks.
goals: Define cohorting rules for prompt sets that surface representative production slices
Specify a composite regression score (quality + safety + latency) and per-signal weighting
Set dynamic thresholds calibrated to historical variability per cohort
Map detected regressions to an action matrix: soft-fail alerts, canary traffic reduction, immediate rollback
Provide well-documented acceptance criteria and telemetry to measure false positive/negative rates
scope_in: Eval harness changes in Optimize that run pre-rollout and continuous post-rollout
Definition of cohort types (user-intent, customer-config, token-length, geographic) and sampling rules
Implementation of composite signal scoring and threshold calibration service
Decision flow engine (rule-based) that enforces traffic shaping and rollback steps
Dashboards and runbooks for on-call and PM visibility
scope_out: Changes to core serving runtime kernels (handled by runtime team) beyond exposing signals
Re-training or model architecture changes — this is about gating and rollbacks only
Billing/chargeback integration for Optimize customers in this iteration
metrics: True positive detection rate of regressions (target >= 90% for P1 regressions)
False positive rollback rate (target <= 1 per 1,000 deploys)
Mean time to detect (MTTD) regressions during canary (target <= 5m)
Mean time to action (MTTA) from signal to first mitigation (target <= 10m)
% of rollbacks triggered by composite score vs single-signal (target >= 80% composite)
acceptance_criteria: Eval harness computes cohort-level composite score and stores per-request signal vectors to traces
Calibrated dynamic thresholds produced from 90-day historical distribution per cohort and are inspectable in the Console
Automated decision flow executes at canary intervals and performs: a) alert-only, b) traffic-shift, c) rollback according to matrix
Dashboards display cohort-level false-positive estimates and daily regression counts
Runbook includes clear escalation steps and an engineer-facing checklist to reproduce a canary regression locally
End-to-end tests cover synthetic regression injection and confirm rollback path executes within the MTTA target
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Unit + integration tests in staging, run synthetic regression injections (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (opt-in customers): Run decision flow in alert-only mode for 2 weeks with selected customers (5-10%)
Phase 2 (canary): Enable traffic-shift actions for 10% canaries for customers who opt in (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (default): Enable full decision flow for all rollouts with automated rollback (gradual ramp over 4 weeks)
Post-launch: 30-day monitoring window and a retro to tune thresholds and weights
monitoring_signals: Quality delta (model A vs model B) measured by evaluation metric suite per-cohort
Safety hits and high-confidence toxicity regressions
Latency P95 and P99 per cohort and per route
Token-efficiency regressions (tokens per useful output) for cost-aware signals
regression_thresholds: Primary composite score: normalized z-score > 3 for cohort over rolling window => signal
Safety: absolute increase in high-confidence safety flags > 0.2% over baseline => immediate alert
Latency: P99 increase > 2x baseline AND correlated with quality loss => escalates decision weight
Small cohorts (n < 1000) use Bayesian posterior credible intervals to avoid noisy z-scores
Thresholds are percentile-based and adapt weekly using exponential decay to prioritize recent traffic
ab_test_criteria: Minimum effective sample size per cohort: 5k requests aggregated or at least 7 days of traffic
Primary gating metric must show statistically significant degradation (p < 0.01) AND effect size > practical delta
Secondary metrics evaluated with hierarchical testing to control family-wise error (safety metrics prioritized)
If different cohorts disagree, follow conservative decision: favor rollback for cohorts with high customer impact labels
rollback_triggers_and_actions: Soft alert: composite score breach but below hard-critical threshold => create ticket, notify owner, no traffic change
Traffic-shift: composite score breach above soft threshold => reduce canary traffic by 50% and continue monitoring for 15 minutes
Immediate rollback: hard threshold breach (e.g., safety critical or composite z > 5) => automatic rollback to previous pinned model and page on-call
Manual override: on-call or PM can escalate to full rollback or abort rollback with a documented justification
Post-rollback: automated incident draft is created and linked to rollback event with key signals attached
decisions: We will use a composite, weighted signal rather than a single metric to reduce noisy rollbacks
Thresholds will be dynamic and cohort-specific, calibrated from 90-day historical distributions
Small-sample cohorts will use Bayesian estimation to avoid overreacting to sparse noise
Initial rollout will be opt-in to collect operating characteristics before defaulting to automatic mitigation
open_questions: What dimension set best defines a 'customer-impact' cohort (account revenue, SLAs, feature flags)?
How do we version the threshold calibration logic and allow safe rollbacks of the decision engine itself?
Do SREs want automated page on immediate rollback or just a high-severity alert?
What retention window for per-request signal traces is cost-acceptable while supporting retrospective investigations?
